messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The test `testRfc4648Section10Encode()` expects the Base64 encoded string for the input "f" to be "Zg==", which is the standard Base64 encoding without chunking. Inspection of the `encodeBase64String(byte[])` method reveals that it calls `encodeBase64(binaryData, true)`, which passes `true` for the `isChunked` parameter. The bug report points out that this should be `false` to avoid chunking the encoded output.

Looking further into `encodeBase64(byte[], boolean)`, it delegates to `encodeBase64(byte[], boolean, boolean)` that ultimately calls the more detailed `encodeBase64(byte[], boolean, boolean, int)`. Inside this method, the boolean parameter `isChunked` determines if the Base64 instance is created with chunking enabled or disabled. When chunking is enabled (`isChunked = true`), the constructor `Base64(urlSafe)` is called, else the constructor `Base64(0, CHUNK_SEPARATOR, urlSafe)` is called, disabling line chunking by setting the chunk length to 0.

Since the public API method `encodeBase64String` currently always passes `true` for `isChunked`, it always chunks its output, producing newlines inserted into the encoded output. This violates the expectation of the test, which wants a continuous Base64 encoded string without chunking.

Thus, the root cause is the incorrect `isChunked` parameter value in `encodeBase64String`. It should be `false` to disable chunking and match the expected output in the test. Changing the call site inside `encodeBase64String` from `encodeBase64(binaryData, true)` to `encodeBase64(binaryData, false)` will fix the issue by producing Base64 encoded strings without inserted newlines.

The bug report explicitly describes this fix and matches the identified cause perfectly. The failure is traced to the method `Base64.encodeBase64String(byte[])`, which is currently enabling chunking when it should not.

Next, I will suggest methods to fix based on this diagnosis.
org.apache.commons.codec.binary.Base64.encodeBase64String(byte[])

Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
